07 FOR NARRATORS & PRODUCERS

Record a voiceover in Limassol.

A museum guide might want a little space between sentences. A line for a finished film has to fit the cut. Bring the script and a reference so you and the technician can listen to a first take together.

Plan a voiceover ↗Session rates ↗

01 SESSION NOTES

Read a paragraph. Listen back. Then roll.

01

Check the room against the brief

We start with a short room-tone sample and a test read on a Shure microphone. If your client has a noise-floor or loudness specification, share it before agreeing the session.

02

Give each pickup a name

Mark any unfamiliar names and words, and number the lines that need choices. For a timed narration, bring a reference video with the cues you need to hit.

03

Choose your audio delivery

A recording of the full read is a different job from a folder of trimmed lines. Tell us how the editor wants the files named, the required format and who will choose the final takes.

02 BEFORE YOU RECORD

Good questions.

Can I record without being filmed?

Yes. Plan an audio-only session and include the length of your script, its language and the number of voices. We’ll quote the recording and any edit separately.

Can I hear the room first?

Ask for a short test recording using the intended mic position. Your producer can check the sample against the needs of the project.

SESSION PLANNER

Put your session on paper.

Choose a starting point and save a brief. Pilot prices and dates are confirmed separately.
